title: Google Sheets
author: Atlas core
description: Read a range, write one, append rows, clear a range, create a spreadsheet, add or delete a sheet, or move the whole file to the trash — through a server-registered Google credential. The operation, the spreadsheet, the range and the values are authored in the model; the credential lives on the server, resolved from the vault (ADR-0235). Values may be a list of rows, one row of cells, or a list of objects written through the Columns given here. A read with Header on answers with objects keyed by the range's first row, which is the shape a multi-instance subprocess iterates. Creating and deleting a spreadsheet are Drive operations on the same credential.

properties.label: Worker
properties.description: Name of the configured Google Sheets Worker (Console → Workers), never a key. The attribute behind this field is spelled connector for compatibility with models already deployed.

properties.label: Spreadsheet (everything but create)
properties.description: The spreadsheet by its id or by the whole URL out of the browser's address bar — both work. Often a FEEL expression naming what an earlier Create spreadsheet wrote, e.g. =datei.spreadsheetId.

properties.label: Title (create)
properties.description: What the new spreadsheet is called.

properties.label: Drive folder (create)
properties.description: Optional. The folder the new spreadsheet is moved into, by id or by the URL of the folder page. The credential must be able to write there — for a service account that usually means the folder is shared with its address.

properties.label: Sheet (create/add sheet/delete sheet)
properties.description: A tab title, as shown on the tab itself. On Create spreadsheet it names the new file's first tab and is optional.

properties.label: Range (read/write/append/clear)
properties.description: A1 notation, optionally naming its sheet (Anträge!A2:F). Without a sheet name Google uses the first tab. For Append rows a whole-column range like Anträge!A:F is usually what you want, since Google appends after the last row that has anything in it.

properties.label: Values (write/append)
properties.description: What to write. A FEEL list of lists is the rows; a flat list is one row; a list of objects is written through the Columns below. A single value writes one cell.

properties.label: Columns (write/append)
properties.description: Only for a list of objects: the fields to write and their order, comma-separated — and the order is the half that has to match the sheet. Without it a list of objects is refused at deploy rather than written in an order nobody chose.

properties.label: Interpret values (write/append)

choices.name: Verbatim — store the text as given

properties.description: As typed is Google's USER_ENTERED: "3,50 €" becomes a currency number and "=SUM(A1:A9)" a formula. Verbatim stores exactly the characters given, which is what an id starting with a zero needs.

properties.label: First row is a header (read)

choices.name: No — answer with the raw rows
Yes — answer with objects keyed by the first row

properties.description: With a header the result is a list of objects (=zeilen[1].name); without it, a list of lists (=zeilen[1][1]). Include the header row in the range when you turn this on.

properties.label: Result variable (everything but the two deletes)
properties.description: Receives what Google returned; a read writes the rows. FEEL lists are 1-based, so the first row is =zeilen[1]. The two deletes answer with nothing a process needs, and the compiler refuses a result variable on them.
